whyThisIsItsOwnFile: packages/assessment cannot grade, and that is structural rather than a convention: AssessmentItemDescriptor has no correctOptionId, no isCorrect on an option, and no rubric, so no bundle built from that package can leak a key. Keeping the key beside the descriptors would put it back. This file is addressed to the grading authority's key table and to nothing else, and verify.mjs fails if a key-shaped field appears in an item file.
destination: packages/grading — the same authority that classifies prose. `GradingAuthority.grade` is async even for selected response precisely because the key lives on the server and not in the form the student is looking at.

releasedItems.policy: Not keyed here. Point the key table at content/staar, where each capture carries `correctAnswerFromOfficialKey` copied from a TEA key document. Copying the letter into this file would give the key two homes and one of them would eventually be wrong.

authoredItems.why: A tax on newspapers and printed paper is the 1765 Stamp Act, not one of the 1774 Coercive Acts. The other three are.
Boston elected its own colonial assembly and no member of Parliament.
On the colonists' own argument, a tax was lawful only from a body they had elected — their own assembly.
Non-importation — agreeing to stop importing British goods — is the economic answer.
A declaration of war is the one form the colonists did NOT take in 1774; the boycott, the petition and the congress are all real forms.
The Continental Congress is the step that turns the closed port into a coordinated boycott.

openResponseItems.policy: No key. The nine open-response items are classified against the binary rubrics carried in items/open-response.json, by the same authority and the same policy the duel uses. A rubric is not a key and must never be flattened into one.

keyingDiscipline.singleCorrect: Every authored item has exactly one defensible answer. No 'best answer' items.
keyingDiscipline.positionBalance: A:2 B:1 C:1 D:2 across the six authored keys. verify.mjs recomputes the distribution and fails if any letter takes more than half the keys.
keyingDiscipline.positionBalanceWhyItMatters: A capstone at 100% per concept is a gate. A student who notices that one letter is usually right does not need the history.
